newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia accepts joint probe on tanker disaster.
newsitem.headline: Russia accepts joint probe on tanker disaster.

text.p: Moscow has agreed to the creation of a joint Russia-Japanese commission to find out what caused the Russian tanker Nakhodka to sink causing widespread pollution off the Japanese coast, Itar-Tass news agency said on Friday.

Tass said Transport Minister Nikolai Tsakh had agreed to a request from Tokyo for cooperation in investigating the sinking on January 2 and offered his direct participation if the Japanese side sent officials of "corresponding rank".

He thanked the Japanese side for rescuing the Nakhodka team and expressed his regrets about the pollution caused by the shipwreck. The loss of the Nakhodka caused some of the worst pollution seen off the Japanese coast and affected important fishing areas.

Tsakh also reiterated that a top Russian commission investigating the wreck of the Nakhodka had determined that the tanker had been in good condition but that it broke in two and sank after hitting a half-submerged ship in heavy seas.
The commission rejected suggestions that the shipwreck had been caused by a mine, by the age of the tanker or by a tidal wave.
Tass earlier quoted Tsakh as saying Tokyo remained convinced that the disaster was caused by a combination of stormy weather and the advanced age of the tanker, which was launched over 25 years ago.
Tsakh said he would provide Japanese authorities with its loading inventory and technical assessments of the Nakhodka's structural condition.
He also said Russia would take part in a tender to lift the tanker's bow and to pump out the oil remaining there.
